ruling: A mix, not a lean (Rulings, Krish, 2026-11-28): every Monday, Wednesday and Friday carries businesses and how AI is changing them under the hood beside individual creators and their tools, and a layered story that carries both is better than either; every Tuesday and Thursday's explainers carry both sides.
line: A mix of businesses and creators, and layered stories that carry both. Each Monday, Wednesday and Friday has a business side (a label, studio, publisher, broadcaster, streamer, platform, agency, club or league, or the AI companies, tools and markets they run on, and what AI is changing in how that business works: how the work is made, sold, priced, licensed or paid for) and a creator side (individual creators, artists and performers and the tools they use). The best stories carry both at once: the business and the people whose work it changes. Neither side takes over a day.

subjects.business: The story is about a company, an industry or a market and what AI changes in how it works: a label's licensing deal, a studio's pipeline, a broadcaster's ad model, a platform's pay-out rule, an AI firm's price that a whole sector runs on.
subjects.creator: The story is about one person (a creator, artist, musician, performer, writer, designer, director or athlete) or one tool feature launched for them, told through what they made or can now do.
subjects.both: The story carries a business and the people who make the work in it, layered: what a label's AI deal does to its artists, how a studio's pipeline changes an animator's job. It counts on each side of the mix.
